你 means “you,” usually addressing one person. Its visible form combines 亻 and 尔, the simplified form of 爾, which was also used for “you/your.” Though 尔 is proposed as a sound cue, the modern readings ěr and nǐ alone do not establish its ancient sound role in 你.
